text:
maria_ops: Heads-up — we're heading into the annual commit talks. Need clarity on two adjacent asks before the call with Raj later today: firm regional availability floors, and how monthly credits are calculated when GPUs are preempted or capacity falls below the floor.

raj_vendor: Thanks Maria. We can discuss both. Quick preview: we offer a regional minimum (soft/firm) + surge pool. Firm floors are often tied to a revenue commitment level. Credits are issued when effective availability < committed floor after agreed measurement windows.

maria_ops: Can you share the exact measurement window and metric? We need something we can pull from our monitoring to reconcile invoices automatically.

raj_vendor: Measurement = "usable GPU hours" per calendar day per region. Window = 30-day rolling. Usable = capacity not preempted and passing health checks for >90% of the minute. If rolled 30d availability < floor -> credit.

sam_vendor: Proposed credit formula we typically use (high level): credit = max(0, (floor - observed)/floor) * committed_monthly_fee * 0.5. The 0.5 is our agreed cap for operational recoverability. Open to negotiation.

oliver_finance: That multiplier is too low for us if we have sustained shortfalls. Can we get a sliding scale: 0.5 up to 5% shortfall, 0.75 for 5-15%, and 1.0 beyond 15%? We'll need that in the term sheet.

jess_eng: Operational point — we need a machine-readable feed (API or prometheus job) that reports per-region "usable_gpu_hours" hourly. Otherwise reconciliation will be a manual nightmare. Raj — can you expose per-AZ metrics and a daily aggregate?

raj_vendor: We can provide an hourly CSV dump via S3 for the committed regions and a Prometheus endpoint for real-time. For billing reconciliation we recommend the CSV as the source of truth.

kevin_sre: Also want a note about preemptible->reserved conversion. If instances are preemptible and then forcibly reclaimed we need a mechanism to convert equivalent quota from the surge pool without a full remediation wait. Otherwise production jobs get killed.

sam_vendor: Surge pool is for short bursts only. For longer preemptions (>12h sustained), we can auto-convert capacity from reserved if you have headroom in other regions or available credits. Need to document thresholds.

maria_ops: Two asks to lock in before contracting: 1) API/data schema for usable_gpu_hours (example payload). 2) A concrete credit table (sliding scale) and an example invoice calculation.

raj_vendor: Example payload (hourly CSV columns): region,timestamp,total_allocated_gpu_hours,preempted_gpu_hours,failed_health_check_hours,usable_gpu_hours

raj_vendor: Example invoice calc — assume committed_monthly_fee = $120k, floor = 2000 usable_gpu_hours/month. Observed = 1700. Shortfall = 300 => 15% shortfall. If sliding scale mapping = 1.0 for >15% then credit = 0.15 * $120k * 1.0 = $18k credit applied next invoice.

oliver_finance: Make sure the credit is line-itemed not netted against other services. We need a separate credit memo for accounting.

lena_legal: We'll need language for measurement disputes (30 day challenge window), audit rights (one audit per year), and force majeure carveouts. Also define what counts as "preemption" vs "maintenance".

maria_ops: Good call. For SRE acceptance criteria: if vendor provides hourly feed + daily aggregate CSV and supports a one-click report we can build a reconciliation job to ingest and reconcile against our internal predictor.

kevin_sre: Suggest adding a health-check rule set to the contract: a GPU is "usable" if agent heartbeat >90% for that minute and driver loaded; otherwise counted as failed_health_check_hours. We'll share the exact probe semantics.

raj_vendor: Acknowledged. We'll draft the technical appendix with probe semantics and sample curl command. Example: curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' 'https://vendor.example.com/usage?region=us-west1&start=2024-06-01T00:00Z&end=2024-06-30T23:00Z'

maria_ops: Any limits to audit log retention? We need 1 year of raw hourly CSVs for invoice disputes.

sam_vendor: We can commit to 12 months retention for the CSV/usage export for committed customers. Longer retention is an add-on.

oliver_finance: Also confirm the billing unit: Is it GPU-hour or vGPU-hour? Our internal reporting is in GPU-hours. Need explicit mapping for fractional GPUs (a.k.a. multi-tenant slices).

raj_vendor: Billing unit = GPU-hour by default. For fractional slices we convert to equivalent GPU-hours using our published factor table (e.g., a 0.25 slice = 0.25 GPU-hour). We'll include conversion rules.

lena_legal: We'll also ask for an early-termination credit schedule if we commit multi-year and vendor misses floor >2 sequential months. Standard carveout: if >2 months under floor, customer may ramp down remaining commitment without penalty after cure period.

maria_ops: Next steps: Raj to send draft term sheet + tech appendix by EOD, legal will redline, finance to verify credit calc, infra to validate feed schema. If that lands, we schedule a final alignment on Thursday.

contractbot: Contract draft created: https://contracts.vendor.com/d/RC-4491. Access: raj_vendor, sam_vendor, lena_legal, oliver_finance, maria_ops.

raj_vendor: Will share EOD. Thanks everyone — we'll try to incorporate the sliding scale and the CSV feed schema in the first pass.

maria_ops: Thanks — we'll prepare reconciliation tests to run on the CSV as soon as we have it. :thumbsup:
